records.title: The five different citation failures
content: A citation can be malformed, point to no source, identify the wrong source, quote inaccurately, or fail to support the proposition. Those are different questions and require different evidence.

A structural parser can reject an impossible reporter series. It cannot establish that a well-formed citation exists, remains good law, or supports the sentence. Write those boundaries before writing code.
records.practice: Classify ten supplied examples by failure layer and write what additional evidence would be needed to resolve each one.

records.title: The verification contract
content: Define accepted inputs, covered citation families, approved sources, possible verdicts, evidence returned, abstention rules, and the person authorized to release work.
The contract must say what a pass means. If only existence was checked, the result must not imply proposition support or current precedential status.
records.practice: Complete a one-page contract with an explicit non-goal for every promised capability.

records.title: Choose the data path before the model
content: Map the document from input through parsing, retrieval, model processing, human review, export, logs, and deletion. Identify every external service and every place confidential material could persist.
Use synthetic or public material until authority, contract, account settings, retention, and supervision are resolved.
records.practice: Draw a data-flow record for a browser-local build and a connected firm build; mark every boundary where information leaves the device.

records.title: Create the review-unit schema
content: A useful review unit stores document ID, claim text, citation string, normalized citation, source snapshot, located passage, verdict, confidence, limitations, reviewer, timestamps, and version.
Keep machine output separate from human disposition. Never overwrite the evidence that produced an earlier result.
records.practice: Create one known-good and one known-bad review record and confirm that another reviewer could reproduce the disposition.

records.title: Build a transparent citation parser
content: Start with a narrow citation family and deterministic patterns. Return the matched text and parsed fields so a learner can see exactly what the parser recognized.
Unknown formats should become unparsed review items, not disappear. Measure extraction recall on the document types you actually expect.
records.practice: Run the public Citation Verifier against the sample, then add five boundary cases and record misses without changing the test labels.

records.title: Bind each citation to the proposition
content: A citation is usually attached to a sentence, clause, quotation, or string of propositions. Capture enough context for review while preserving the exact proposition being tested.
When one sentence contains multiple claims or citations, split the review units or mark the mapping ambiguous. Do not let proximity silently become support.
records.practice: Annotate a paragraph containing three claims and two citations; explain every claim-to-citation boundary.

records.title: Rank sources by authority and purpose
content: Use official court or government material when the task requires an authoritative rule or filing. Research databases and aggregators may be useful for discovery but have different coverage, licensing, status, and citator boundaries.
Record which source answered which question. A source that establishes existence may not establish current validity.
records.practice: Create an approved-source hierarchy for one jurisdiction and define the fallback when the preferred source is unavailable.

records.title: Retrieve, normalize, and preserve
content: Normalize the query, preserve the original citation, log the source and retrieval time, and return zero, one, or multiple candidates without forcing a match.
Store a permitted snapshot or stable reference to the reviewed material. Respect authentication, rate limits, licensing, and redistribution restrictions.
records.practice: Design the response for no match, one match, and ambiguous matches; require a human choice whenever identity is uncertain.

records.title: Locate the supporting passage
content: Retrieve candidate passages around meaningful terms, quotations, headings, and citations. Preserve page or paragraph locators where the source provides them.
Retrieval is a candidate-generation step. The best-scoring passage is not proof that the proposition is supported.
records.practice: For three propositions, return the strongest candidate passage and one plausible distractor; explain why ranking alone cannot issue the verdict.

records.title: Compare claim, qualification, and conflict
content: Test who, what, when, jurisdiction, conditions, degree, and exceptions. A source may support a narrower proposition while the draft overstates it.
Require the system to quote the passage, identify the mismatch, and abstain when context is incomplete. A model explanation without inspectable source text is not a verification result.
records.practice: Rewrite three overstated claims to the strongest formulation their sources actually support.

records.title: Use a verdict taxonomy that cannot hide uncertainty
content: Use bounded labels such as structurally invalid, no source located, identity ambiguous, supported, supported with qualification, contradicted, unsupported, and not verified.
Confidence describes the basis for a provisional result; it does not convert missing evidence into support.
records.practice: Assign verdicts to twelve cases and write the permitted next action for each label.

records.title: Produce an inspectable review report
content: A reviewer needs the proposition, original citation, normalized record, source link, passage, verdict, reason, unresolved issue, reviewer status, and version in one place.
Separate machine suggestion, reviewer decision, and release decision. Make changes traceable.
records.practice: Create a one-page report that lets a supervisor disagree with the result without rerunning the system.

records.title: Keep professional responsibility with the professional
content: ABA Formal Opinion 512 applies existing competence, confidentiality, communication, supervision, candor, and fee duties to lawyers using generative AI. Rule 11 separately governs representations made by presenting a paper in federal civil litigation.
The verifier assists inquiry. It does not become the lawyer, editor, researcher, or accountable releaser.
records.practice: Identify the named approver, prohibited inputs, escalation triggers, and release evidence for a high-stakes filing workflow.

records.title: Design the audit and change record
content: Record the document hash or version, tool version, ruleset, sources checked, timestamps, results, overrides, reviewer, and release status.
Log enough to reconstruct the decision without retaining confidential content longer than the approved policy permits.
records.practice: Draft an audit record and retention rule that distinguish evidentiary need from indiscriminate storage.

records.title: Build the failure-focused test set
content: Construct representative cases for valid citations, malformed forms, nonexistent authorities, wrong metadata, inaccurate quotations, overstatement, contradiction, ambiguous mapping, unavailable sources, and unsupported formats.
Keep test labels independent of the system being tested and document the coverage boundary.
records.practice: Create at least twenty labeled cases, including cases designed to expose false passes.

records.title: Measure dangerous errors
content: Report results by failure class. False passes are especially consequential because they create unwarranted assurance; false flags create review burden and may also hide systematic gaps.
Do not publish a single accuracy number without the dataset, denominator, labels, version, coverage, and error distribution.
records.practice: Calculate the confusion matrix for each verdict family and write the release decision those results justify.

records.title: Choose prototype, pilot, or deployment
content: A local demonstration, connected research pilot, governed workflow, and institutional system have different evidence, security, integration, and operational requirements.
Release only the capability level that was actually tested. Document exclusions and the conditions required to move to the next level.
records.practice: Write a deployment decision memo with a precise status label, permitted users, permitted data, known limitations, and rollback trigger.

records.title: Defend the system without overselling it
content: Present the verifier through its contract, architecture, evidence, test results, limitations, human gate, and change plan. Demonstrate one success and one abstention.
A credible defense explains what the system cannot establish and shows how the workflow responds when evidence is missing.
records.practice: Record a ten-minute capstone defense and answer the rubric questions using only evidence in the project package.

editorialSections.title: A fake citation is no longer a small mistake

blocks.text: Courts have sanctioned lawyers for filings containing fabricated and mis-stated authorities. "It sounded right" is not a verification method. For anyone who publishes sourced claims — lawyers, clerks, researchers, journalists, and policy writers — an unverified citation creates professional risk.

The problem is not just whether a source exists. It is whether the source actually supports the specific proposition it is cited for. That is the gap this course teaches you to close, with a tool you build and control.

editorialSections.title: A verifier that checks the claim, not just the link

blocks.text: The public course teaches you to build or specify a bounded system that takes a document and its citations and returns a per-citation review record with evidence. A working deployment depends on the learner's implementation, approved sources, testing, and human-review environment.
Every citation and its claim
Pulls each citation and the exact proposition it is cited for.
Exists and supports
Confirms the source is real and retrievable, then whether it actually supports the claim.
Fabricated, mis-stated, unsupported
A verdict per citation with the supporting passage or the gap.
A shareable audit
Verdicts, evidence, and confidence, ready to hand to a supervisor.
An audit trail
Every check recorded, so it is provable and not merely asserted.
Human signs off
On doubt it defaults to flag for review. You stay accountable; the tool assists.

summary: Build and document a bounded claims-review prototype for marketing, product, and label copy. All nine modules and eighteen lessons are public; enrollment, submissions, grading, credentials, a connected regulatory system, and the planned tutor are not available.
audience: Marketing, product, compliance, and regulatory teams whose public claims may be reviewed by regulators.

records.title: Bound the product, audience, and jurisdiction
Map claims to rules and evidence
Design human review and change control
Package the checker and its evidence
Separate claim types before screening
content: A review begins by identifying the representation a reasonable audience may take from the complete communication. Express wording, implication, imagery, omissions, comparisons, testimonials, and product context can create different claims.
Do not collapse every claim into a generic risk score. Record the precise representation, audience, product, medium, jurisdiction, and decision date before asking what evidence it needs.
records.practice: Annotate a sample product page into discrete claim records and explain whether each representation is express, implied, comparative, testimonial, or omitted-context dependent.

records.title: Write the checker contract
content: Define accepted inputs, covered products and jurisdictions, approved authority sources, disposition labels, abstention rules, required evidence, reviewer roles, and prohibited uses.
A screen is not regulatory approval. The contract must state which questions the checker can answer and which require qualified legal, regulatory, scientific, or medical review.
records.practice: Draft a one-page operating contract with a non-goal and escalation trigger for every advertised capability.

records.title: Resolve product, audience, channel, and jurisdiction
content: The same sentence can face different rules when used for a drug, supplement, cosmetic, food, device, service, or general consumer product. Audience and channel also change the surrounding impression.
If classification, intended use, jurisdiction, or audience is unresolved, the checker must abstain from a final disposition and route the record to a qualified reviewer.
records.practice: Complete the scope fields for three versions of one claim and identify which unresolved fact prevents rule mapping.

records.title: Create the claim-review record
content: A reproducible review unit preserves the source creative, exact claim, surrounding context, audience, product class, jurisdiction, authority version, evidence supplied, machine suggestion, human disposition, limitations, owner, and timestamps.
Keep the original claim and evidence snapshot immutable. Corrections should create a new version rather than erase what the earlier reviewer saw.
records.practice: Create one complete review record and ask another person to reproduce its scope decision using only the stored fields.

records.title: Extract express claims without losing context
content: Start with deterministic segmentation of headings, body copy, captions, calls to action, labels, footnotes, and visible qualifications. Preserve the exact span and its location.
A parser should return uncertain or compound spans for review instead of silently deleting them. Extraction coverage must be tested on the formats the organization actually publishes.
records.practice: Extract every express claim from a sample advertisement and record three boundary cases that require human segmentation.

records.title: Test the net impression for implied claims
content: An implied claim may arise from words, images, demonstrations, omissions, sequence, or the relationship among statements. The unit of review is the communication's net impression, not isolated grammar.
Models may propose possible implications, but the record must show the concrete elements producing the interpretation and allow a reviewer to reject it.
records.practice: List the express and implied takeaways from a health-product ad and tie each implied claim to the exact creative elements that produce it.

records.title: Rank authorities by question and date
content: Statutes, regulations, binding orders, official labeling rules, and agency guidance do not carry identical legal force. Record authority type, jurisdiction, effective date, scope, and the exact question it answers.
A search result or model summary is discovery material, not the rule record. Prefer current official text and preserve the retrieval date and supersession status.
records.practice: Build a five-source hierarchy for one product category and document what happens when the preferred authority is silent or outdated.

records.title: Turn authority into inspectable rule records
content: Each rule record should identify the source, quoted or accurately paraphrased requirement, covered claim class, prerequisites, exceptions, required qualification, evidence expectation, reviewer, and version.
Separate the authority's language from internal policy. An organization may adopt a stricter release rule, but the record must not misattribute that choice to a regulator.
records.practice: Create two authority-backed rule records and one clearly labeled internal-policy record for the same campaign.

records.title: Map each claim to the governing question
content: Rule mapping is a reasoned join among the claim, product classification, intended use, audience, medium, jurisdiction, and authority scope. Keyword overlap alone cannot establish that a rule governs.
Return every plausible rule, the mapping rationale, conflicts, and missing scope facts. Require human resolution when multiple regimes or product classifications remain possible.
records.practice: Map five claim records to rule records and document why one tempting keyword match is inapplicable.

records.title: Match the claim to the evidence actually held
content: Evidence must fit the exact product, population, outcome, magnitude, timing, conditions, and level of certainty expressed. Related research does not automatically substantiate the advertised representation.
Record the evidence supplied, its limitations, and the qualified professional's assessment. The checker should identify missing evidence dimensions rather than invent a universal proof threshold.
records.practice: Compare three claims with a supplied evidence summary and rewrite each to the strongest formulation the record may support.

records.title: Use dispositions that preserve uncertainty
content: Use bounded labels such as ready for qualified review, evidence missing, qualification required, potential prohibition, scope unresolved, authority conflict, and not assessed.
A probability or confidence score cannot convert absent evidence into approval. Each disposition needs a rationale, supporting record, limitation, and permitted next action.
records.practice: Assign dispositions to ten claim-evidence pairs and specify the evidence or decision needed to move each record forward.

records.title: Produce a review report a human can challenge
content: A useful report places the claim, context, governing question, authority, evidence, provisional disposition, rationale, uncertainty, reviewer status, and version together.
Separate extraction, automated suggestion, subject-matter review, legal or regulatory review, and release approval so later readers know who decided what.
records.practice: Design a one-page report that allows an approver to disagree with a suggestion without rerunning or overwriting the record.

records.title: Route consequential uncertainty to named people
content: Escalation rules should name the owner for product classification, scientific support, legal interpretation, medical review, brand approval, and final release. A generic human-in-the-loop label is insufficient.
Block release when a required field, authority, evidence record, reviewer, or approval is missing. Preserve disagreement rather than forcing consensus into one score.
records.practice: Build an escalation matrix for six failure states, including the accountable role, required evidence, response condition, and release block.

records.title: Version the rules, evidence, and decisions
content: Record content version, rule-library version, evidence version, model or parser version, timestamps, automated output, overrides, approvers, and release state.
Retention must follow an approved policy. Store enough to reconstruct the decision without collecting unrelated personal, confidential, or regulated data.
records.practice: Draft an audit event schema and a change rule for authority updates, evidence withdrawal, and revised campaign copy.

records.title: Build a representative claims test set
content: Include supportable claims, missing-evidence cases, subtle implication, required qualifications, scope ambiguity, authority conflict, and examples that must be escalated.
Freeze expected labels before tuning. Keep product classes, channels, jurisdictions, and difficulty visible so aggregate performance cannot hide a dangerous subgroup.
records.practice: Create a twenty-item test set with adjudicated expected dispositions and a reason each item belongs.

records.title: Measure false assurance and review burden
content: Track extraction misses, incorrect rule mappings, unsupported ready signals, missed escalation, over-flagging, reviewer disagreement, and unresolved cases. False assurance is more consequential than fluent wording.
Report the test set, denominator, version, known gaps, and subgroup results. Do not publish an accuracy claim that extends beyond the evaluated corpus.
records.practice: Write an evaluation report with a release threshold, stop condition, and remediation owner for every material failure type.

records.title: Package a bounded open-material prototype
content: Package the operating contract, claim schema, authority register, rule library, evidence model, dispositions, reviewer matrix, test set, evaluation, change log, and limitations with the prototype.
A browser-local or demonstration build is not a production compliance system. Release language must match the tested data path, integrations, maintenance, and accountable organization.
records.practice: Assemble the capstone evidence packet and mark every dependency that remains unavailable or unverified.

records.title: Defend the decision without overstating it
content: A defensible presentation demonstrates what the checker found, what evidence it used, where it abstained, how humans decided, and which failures remain.
The final decision is whether this bounded system may assist a defined review step—not whether AI can approve regulated claims generally.
records.practice: Present one correct result, one false positive, one missed issue, and one abstention; explain the resulting release decision.

editorialSections.title: A claim you can't back up is a bill waiting to arrive

blocks.text: Regulators are active right now. The FTC opens cases over unsubstantiated health, performance, and green claims; the FDA sends warning letters over disease and structure-function language; state AGs and platforms pull listings and ads that overstate. A single line of copy that promises more than your evidence supports can trigger a penalty, a warning letter, or a takedown.

The hard part is not knowing rules exist. It is catching the specific claim, mapping it to the specific rule, and knowing what proof it needs, before the copy goes live. That is the gap this course teaches you to close, with a tool you build and own.

Choose a bounded, reversible workflow
content: Choose one recurring workflow with a clear trigger, known inputs, a reviewable output, and a human owner. Prefer a low-consequence task that can be rerun or discarded without sending, spending, publishing, changing a system of record, or exposing sensitive data.

State the non-goal as carefully as the goal. The first team should not replace a job, decide a person's rights, interpret professional obligations, or take an external action. It should prepare bounded work for review.
records.practice: Write a Workflow Contract naming the trigger, owner, input class, desired output, prohibited outcomes, reversibility condition, and the exact event that ends the run.

records.title: Map trigger, inputs, steps, decisions, output, and owner
content: Map the work as it exists before assigning agents: trigger, accepted inputs, transformations, decision points, sources of truth, handoffs, output, approval, and accountable owner. Record where judgment, confidential information, or external authority enters.

Do not automate around an unknown process. A handoff is complete only when the next role receives a defined record, can tell what has and has not been checked, and knows what must happen when required information is missing.
records.practice: Create a one-page workflow map and mark every consequential decision, sensitive input, external action, and unresolved dependency.

records.title: Classify steps as off-limits, augment, or automate
content: Classify each workflow step separately. Off-limits means the system may not perform or infer the step. Augment means it may prepare options or a draft while a named person decides. Automate means a deterministic, reversible action may run inside explicit limits.

Use augmentation as the default. Increase authority only after representative testing shows the step is bounded, observable, recoverable, and owned. A capable model is not evidence that a particular use is appropriate.
records.practice: Complete an authority table for every mapped step and justify any step placed above augmentation.

records.title: Design the human-control and stop conditions
content: Human review is a control only when the reviewer has time, competence, evidence, authority, and a real ability to reject or change the output. Name the approval object, approver, evidence shown, allowed decisions, and what the system does while approval is absent.

The first team must stop before sending, spending, publishing, executing transactions, modifying authoritative records, or granting access. Define timeout, cancellation, escalation, and rollback behavior rather than relying on a vague human-in-the-loop label.
records.practice: Write a Human Control record with the approval object, named owner, minimum evidence, approve/reject/revise choices, timeout, escalation, and recovery rule.

records.title: Create roles from work, not personas
content: Split the workflow where responsibilities, evidence needs, or review standards differ. A role exists because it owns a bounded transformation—not because a team diagram needs more characters. One role may research, another draft, and another check, but none should approve its own consequential work.

For every role, record purpose, accepted inputs, permitted methods, required sources, output schema, quality checks, prohibited acts, escalation triggers, and accountable human. Name the role only after that contract is coherent.
records.practice: Draft Agent Role Contracts for the smallest useful team and remove any role whose work cannot be distinguished, tested, or owned.

records.title: Limit tools, data, memory, and handoffs
content: Grant each role only the data, tools, actions, and retention it needs for the current step. Separate read, draft, recommend, write, send, publish, purchase, delete, and administer permissions. A prompt prohibition is not an access control.

Treat every inter-agent message, retrieved document, tool result, and user instruction as data with provenance and trust limits. Handoffs should preserve source references, uncertainty, validation status, and the next role's permitted action.
records.practice: Build a Permission Matrix covering roles, data classes, tools, allowed actions, denied actions, retention, escalation, and the human who may change each permission.

records.title: Run representative cases and preserve evidence
content: Test normal, ambiguous, incomplete, adversarial, and prohibited cases. Preserve the input class, system and rule versions, outputs, sources, handoffs, approvals, failures, corrections, latency, and cost needed to reproduce the judgment.

A successful demonstration is not a release decision. Evaluate task completion, unsupported claims, source fidelity, boundary violations, permission attempts, handoff loss, reviewer burden, recovery, and whether the human approval step caught consequential failure.
records.practice: Run at least five representative cases and record each in an Evidence Ledger without inserting confidential or personal information into the public course record.

records.title: Package the supervised workflow and make a go/no-go decision
content: Package the workflow map, role contracts, permission matrix, human-control record, evidence ledger, known limitations, incident and rollback procedure, owner, and review date. The package must let another person understand what the team may do and challenge the evidence for expanding it.

Choose stop, revise, continue as supervised, or propose a separately reviewed expansion. Do not infer production readiness from course completion. Live tools, sensitive data, external actions, or money require technical controls, organizational authorization, security review, and monitoring beyond this open course.

records.title: Name the use case and consequence
content: A knowledge base is ready only for a defined use case, audience, decision, and consequence. A collection may support low-risk discovery while remaining unfit for customer, legal, clinical, personnel, or financial answers.
Write accepted uses, prohibited uses, accountable owners, expected evidence, and the conditions that require abstention or escalation before evaluating documents.
records.practice: Write a one-page use-case contract with users, questions, consequences, owners, non-goals, and stop conditions.

records.title: Write the readiness rubric
content: Define observable criteria for authority, coverage, freshness, structure, conflict, access, and evaluation. Do not collapse them into one reassuring score.
Set fail-closed rules for missing owners, unresolved conflicts, prohibited data, and untested consequential uses. Preserve unknown and not-applicable states.
records.practice: Create a criterion-level rubric with evidence fields, owners, thresholds, and hard-stop rules.

records.title: Create the source register
content: Inventory each candidate source by stable identifier, title, system, format, owner, audience, authority, review date, access class, and disposition. A folder listing is not enough.
Use metadata and document sampling to find shadow copies, exports, attachments, embedded media, inaccessible scans, and sources that lack a responsible owner.
records.practice: Register a representative collection and mark every missing field as unresolved rather than guessing.

records.title: Resolve authority and ownership
content: Authoritative means authorized for the stated question, not merely recent or frequently accessed. Record which source controls when policies, contracts, manuals, FAQs, and working notes disagree.
Assign a content owner and a system owner. Unowned sources cannot silently become organizational truth.
records.practice: Create an authority hierarchy and route five ambiguous sources to named owners for disposition.

records.title: Build the expected-question map
content: Coverage must be tested against questions the system is expected to answer. Gather representative questions across roles, vocabulary, task stages, edge cases, and consequential decisions.
For each question, record the expected answer, approved evidence, acceptable abstention, and reviewer. Do not infer coverage from document volume.
records.practice: Create twenty representative question records with expected evidence and risk classification.

records.title: Record gaps without fabricating answers
content: A gap exists when no approved source supports the expected answer, the evidence covers only part of the question, or the organization has not made the underlying decision.
Distinguish missing content, missing policy, inaccessible evidence, ambiguous ownership, and out-of-scope questions because each requires a different remedy.
records.practice: Classify each uncovered question and assign an owner, remedy, due date, or explicit exclusion.

records.title: Measure freshness with evidence
content: File modification time does not prove substantive review. Preserve effective date, last reviewed date, reviewer, review basis, superseding source, and next review trigger.
Set different freshness expectations by source type and consequence. A stable glossary and a changing procedure should not share an arbitrary age threshold.
records.practice: Define evidence-based freshness rules for five source classes and test them against the register.

records.title: Design review, supersession, and retirement
content: Every included source needs a review trigger, owner, supersession rule, archive treatment, and deletion or retention basis. Retrieval should not treat current and retired versions as peers.
Document what happens when ownership changes, a review is missed, or an upstream policy changes. Default affected material to review rather than silently serving it.
records.practice: Create a lifecycle rule and simulate a missed review and a superseding policy.

records.title: Create addressable content units
content: Prepare content units that preserve headings, definitions, exceptions, tables, citations, and relationships. Chunking that severs a condition from its rule can produce a fluent but wrong answer.
Record parsing failures, scans, images, multi-column layouts, embedded files, and other formats that require transformation or exclusion.
records.practice: Transform and inspect ten representative units, preserving source location and necessary context.

records.title: Preserve metadata and provenance
content: Every retrievable unit should point back to its authoritative source, version, owner, access class, effective dates, and exact location. Derived summaries require their own provenance and review state.
Use stable identifiers so corrections, exclusions, and evaluation failures can be traced to the units that produced them.
records.practice: Define the metadata contract and verify that ten units can be reconstructed from their records.

records.title: Separate copies from competing sources
content: Exact duplicates, near-duplicates, localized variants, historical versions, and independently authoritative sources are different states. Similarity alone cannot decide which one governs.
Group related documents, preserve lineage, and require an owner to approve canonical, supporting, historical, excluded, or unresolved status.
records.practice: Resolve a duplicate cluster without deleting evidence of lineage or unresolved authority.

records.title: Route contradictions to human owners
content: Contradictions may involve rules, dates, definitions, thresholds, exceptions, or scope. Automated detection can surface candidates but cannot invent the organization's controlling decision.
Record both passages, source authority, affected questions, consequence, owner, disposition, and review evidence. Exclude unresolved consequential conflicts from answer generation.
records.practice: Create conflict records for five cases and test whether each affected question abstains or escalates.

records.title: Classify sensitive and restricted content
content: Inventory personal, confidential, privileged, regulated, contractual, security-sensitive, and secret-bearing content under the organization's actual policies and obligations.
Automated detectors are fallible. Treat their output as candidates for authorized review; preserve false-negative risk and do not claim that scanning proves a collection safe.
records.practice: Write classification and escalation rules using synthetic examples; do not upload real sensitive documents to course tools.

records.title: Enforce access before retrieval
content: Retrieval must respect source authorization, user identity, purpose, tenancy, and current permission. Filtering after generation is too late because restricted content may already have entered model context or logs.
Test deny-by-default behavior, permission changes, revoked users, cached results, citations, exports, logs, and administrative access.
records.practice: Create a role-resource matrix and run allowed, denied, revoked, cross-role, and stale-cache cases.

records.title: Build the retrieval evaluation set
content: Create representative, edge, adversarial, permission, conflict, stale-source, and no-answer cases before evaluating a system. Predeclare expected evidence, expected answer boundary, and required abstention.
Keep retrieval and answer evaluation distinct: relevant evidence can be missed, irrelevant evidence retrieved, or correct evidence transformed into an unsupported answer.
records.practice: Build a thirty-case evaluation set with risk tags and expected outcomes.

records.title: Interpret results without a false readiness score
content: Report failures by use case and control: retrieval coverage, evidence precision, citation traceability, answer support, abstention, permission enforcement, freshness, and conflict handling.
Averages can hide critical failures. Preserve every consequential miss, unauthorized retrieval, unsupported answer, and failure to abstain as a release blocker until reviewed.
records.practice: Produce a case-level results table and a narrative explaining where the collection is and is not ready.

records.title: Prioritize the remediation backlog
content: Translate gaps into bounded work: decide policy, appoint owner, update source, resolve conflict, repair format, change permission, add evaluation, exclude material, or narrow the use case.
Rank by consequence and dependency, not document count. Record acceptance evidence and a responsible decision-maker for each item.
records.practice: Create a prioritized backlog with owner, evidence, dependency, due date, and disposition.

records.title: Issue a scoped go, conditional go, or no-go
content: A readiness decision applies only to the tested collection, use case, permissions, configuration, evaluation set, and date. It is not a certification of the organization or a guarantee of accurate answers.
State included and excluded sources, unresolved risks, monitoring triggers, owners, rollback, review date, and the changes that void the decision.
records.practice: Issue a bounded decision packet and defend each limitation with evidence.

editorialSections.title: Questions

blocks.text: Do I need to know how to code?

No code is required to complete the evidence method and browser-local self-assessment. Implementing ingestion, access enforcement, retrieval, evaluation automation, or production deployment requires the relevant technical and security capabilities.
Do I need a RAG system already?

No. The course evaluates a bounded collection before retrieval. Its conclusions apply only to the sampled sources, stated use case, permissions, evidence, and date; they do not establish organization-wide readiness.
What about sensitive data?

Classification, access, and escalation are core steps, but automated detection is fallible. Do not upload real sensitive documents to the public course tools. Authorized security, privacy, legal, compliance, and information owners remain responsible for the governing rules and release decision.
What is the AI tutor?

A planned course assistant intended to answer from reviewed materials and cite the relevant lesson. It is not currently connected or available; its scope and refusal behavior must be evaluated before release.

Course terms and refund policy to be finalized before launch.

records.title: Build a Legislative and Regulatory Tracker
Define tracked and material
records.summary: A tracker begins with an explicit promise: named jurisdictions, authority types, topics, event types, collection cadence, known exclusions, and a review date. “Tracked” means only that the stated collection and review steps ran; it does not mean every legal development was found.

records.title: Build the source and record workspace
records.summary: For every source, preserve jurisdiction, publisher, collection, endpoint or page, authentication, rate limits, update behavior, identifiers, available text versions, expected latency, terms, owner, and last successful check. A URL alone is not an operating source.

records.title: Bound the watch list
records.summary: Do not turn “fifty states plus federal agencies” into an unbounded build. Select jurisdictions because a named decision depends on them, identify the legislative and administrative instruments in scope, and obtain review of local process and terminology.

records.title: Collect without claiming completeness
records.summary: Prefer documented APIs, bulk data, feeds, or official notifications, but verify what each interface omits and how it represents updates. Capture pagination, windows, time zones, identifiers, corrections, withdrawals, and endpoint changes; never infer legal status from HTTP success.

records.title: Detect and classify change
records.summary: Store retrieved versions rather than only the latest text. Normalize presentation cautiously, calculate a digest, retain the original artifact, and compare structurally meaningful units. Cosmetic differences, corrected metadata, substituted text, and legal amendments require different labels.

records.title: Summarize from the source
records.summary: A useful alert states what document changed, the exact compared versions, what text or status changed, what remains unknown, and why a defined audience may care. It does not convert procedural movement into legal effect or predict impact without reviewed evidence.

records.title: Score and route with reasons
records.summary: Relevance and urgency are organizational judgments. Use separate, inspectable factors such as subject match, affected entity, stage, deadline, geographic scope, operational dependency, reversibility, and evidence confidence. Unknown data must not receive a reassuring default score.

records.title: Review, release, and recover

records.title: Test, document, and decide
records.summary: Use a dated set of known changes plus negative and ambiguous cases. Never publish a universal accuracy claim from one test set.

title: Audit Any Business for AI-Readiness
summary: Build a bounded, evidence-backed method for mapping workflows, separating value from feasibility and consequence, classifying governance requirements, prioritizing reversible pilots, and producing a reviewable roadmap. All nine modules and eighteen lessons are public; no audit service, universal readiness determination, enrollment, grading, or credential is provided.
audience: Consultants, operators, transformation leaders, and internal AI owners who need a repeatable adoption method.
learningPaths: Define the decision and audit boundary
evidence: Dated audit scope, workflow register, and source register
Representative inputs, outputs, policies, systems, exceptions, and failure cases
Score rationales, uncertainty, dissent, evaluation evidence, approvals, and roadmap decisions
methodology: Separate value, feasibility, consequence, and confidence
Keep critical controls outside composite scores
Prioritize reversible pilots with explicit evaluation gates
Turn findings into owned decisions and review dates
assumptions: Authorized workflow owners and affected participants provide representative evidence
Qualified domain, privacy, security, legal, and technical reviewers are available where the use requires them
limitations: The method cannot establish universal or certified AI-readiness and does not replace industry-specific professional review
Findings are only as reliable as the bounded evidence, participation, authority records, and evaluation available on the review date
editorialIntro: Build a bounded audit evidence packet for a named organizational decision. records.title: Bounded AI-readiness audit evidence packet
records.brief: Audit one named decision across a bounded workflow set using authorized evidence. Produce defensible findings and a roadmap without representing the result as universal readiness, certification, guaranteed ROI, or professional approval.
evidenceRequirements: Dated scope, exclusions, reliance boundary, participants, owners, and source register

Pilot contract, baseline, evaluation set, thresholds, review, incident, and rollback plan
Sequenced roadmap with no-go findings, dependencies, owners, costs, review dates, and release approval

records.title: Audit evidence self-review

criteria.name: Boundary
criteria.standard: Decision, scope, exclusions, evidence date, reliance, and owners are explicit.

criteria.name: Traceability
criteria.standard: Every finding resolves to representative evidence and source identity.

criteria.name: Decision quality
criteria.standard: Dimensions, confidence, blocks, alternatives, dissent, and uncertainty remain separate.

criteria.name: Human control
criteria.standard: Authority, affected people, review, incident, correction, and stop conditions are assigned.

records.scoringMethod: Weighted self-review; any missing scope, representative evidence, critical control, affected-person review, or release authority blocks completion.

records.title: Bounded audit release rubric

criteria.name: Workflow evidence
criteria.standard: Workflow records reflect actual work, variation, exceptions, systems, and owners.

criteria.name: Scoring integrity
criteria.standard: Value, feasibility, consequence, confidence, and blocks are evidenced and separable.

criteria.name: Governance
criteria.standard: Data, access, authority, rights, security, legal, and recordkeeping questions are resolved or blocking.

criteria.name: Evaluation
criteria.standard: Baselines, representative and adverse cases, thresholds, incidents, and rollback are testable.

criteria.name: Roadmap
criteria.standard: No-go, repair, pilot, and scale decisions are sequenced with owners and review dates.

records.scoringMethod: Weighted self-review plus blocking critical controls; a composite score cannot override missing evidence, authority, safety, or approval.
